subject: biology-2
question: The **endosymbiotic theory** says mitochondria and chloroplasts began as free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by a larger cell. Which line of evidence best supports this theory?

options.text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain no DNA of their own.
The ribosomes inside mitochondria are identical to the ribosomes in the surrounding cytoplasm.
Mitochondria have two membranes, just like every other organelle in the cell.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own circular DNA and divide on their own, similar to bacteria.

explanation: Endosymbiosis predicts that engulfed bacteria would keep bacterial traits, and mitochondria and chloroplasts show them all: their own circular DNA, self-division, double membranes, and ribosomes that resemble bacterial ones. D names the evidence that best supports the theory. A contradicts the known DNA content of these organelles, B misstates the ribosome comparison, and C is false because most organelles have a single membrane.
